description: PEER_REVIEWED (published version: Journal of Finance 79(2), 2024). PROVENANCE CAVEAT: the text read was the June 2018 working paper, NOT the published JF version -- figures may differ in the published paper and have not been re-checked against it. Sample Jan 1994 - Dec 2014, nine G10 currencies vs USD (AUD CAD EUR JPY NZD NOK SEK CHF GBP). INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION of the Breedon-Ranaldo direction with seven additional years of data: during US trading hours 8:30am-5:00pm EST foreign currencies APPRECIATE against USD (i.e. USD depreciates in its own local hours), 'ranging between 8.54% (CHF) and 1.51% (CAD)', the yen the sole exception at -2.01%. SOURCE_STATED after costs: 'an equally-weighted portfolio consisting of only these three currency pairs [CHF, EUR, GBP] generates, on average, 3.29% after accounting for transaction costs.' Stability: results 'are robust to...the choice of the sample period.' This is the only SOURCE_STATED explicit clock window found: 8:30am-5:00pm EST for the US session. UNKNOWN: local windows for the non-US sessions; the transaction cost model used. Sample ends 2014 -- 12 years stale as of registration.
title: FX Premia Around the Clock (working paper; published as 'Foreign Exchange Fixings and Returns around the Clock', Journal of Finance 2024)
